genResearchMaterialEmpty: No research materials yet. Add one first.
genResearchMaterialNoText: This material has no text yet; a generation only gets its title and source.
genResearchMaterialSingle: One run reads at most one material. To combine several sources, generate once per material.
imagePromptPlaceholder: Describe an image for AI to generate
imageGenerateNoModel: The selected image provider has no image-generation models. In Settings pick an image provider that supports generation (OpenAI or Gemini), or use the online image search below.
imageEstimateHint: Asked of the server and read-only: the same price catalog, budget settings and ledger the call's own check uses, so this preview cannot disagree with the check that would refuse the call. The prompt is not sent, no amount is held and no ledger row is written.
imageEstimateBlockedHint: The check that runs at call time is the one that decides: raise the limit, or declare a price for this dimension, if the call has to go through.
imageEstimatePriceHint: No price on file for this dimension, so the amount cannot be stated - which is not the same as free. Declaring one under System Settings, Available Models, Price catalog makes this figure computable.
imageSearchHint: Filter the library by name. Fuzzy matches part of the name, exact matches the whole name.

publishDraftEmpty: The platform page took none of the content, so no draft was prepared. Open the platform once, adjust its publish settings in Account Management, then try again.
publishDraftLoginRequired: The platform is asking you to sign in. Log the account in again in Account Management, then publish.
publishCloseConfirm: This run is still open: closing now stops the browser session and discards the platform draft.
publishDebugRecordHint: Persist the step log and screenshots to disk (artifacts/publish-logs); turn it on before the next run.

publishEmptyAccounts: No accounts yet. Add and log in one first in Account Management.

vcTooLarge: This video is larger than the 5 GB limit.

vcPlatformEmptyTitle: Pick publish accounts first, then configure platform settings

loginIframeHint: Click in the preview below and type your credentials to log in. The session is saved locally (until it expires or is cleared).
loginTypeHint: Type text (first click the target input in the preview, then send)
riskHint: Checks every account headlessly: it opens the publishing page in the saved browser profile and reports whether a sign-in wall is showing. Nothing is clicked, typed or published.
riskAllHealthy: No account needs attention right now.
riskEmptyHint: Run a health check to verify the sign-in state of every account.
riskReasonSessionExpired: Recent failures look like an expired session
accountEmptyFiltered: No accounts match the current filters
addAccountPickPlatformHint: Choose a platform. A browser window opens so you can scan the QR code or sign in, and the account is saved automatically.
addAccountWaiting: Waiting for sign-in to complete… ({seconds}s left)
addAccountBrowserHint: Complete the sign-in in the opened browser window. When it is done, the account is saved and this dialog closes automatically.
addAccountTimeout: Sign-in timed out. The account is saved as "login required".
accountGroupManageHint: Rename a group to update every account in it, or delete it to ungroup them.
cmsPairingBody: A pairing code can be used only once and stays valid for 10 minutes. The connection token is stored encrypted — no database backup or admin password is required. The site also counts toward your account quota, while CMS publishing uses a separate daily allowance; each successful write (draft included) counts once per site.
usageCardNote: Only successfully generated articles are counted. Token usage is tracked separately; the figures above reflect the full successful-call totals.
usageTableNote: Only successful generations are counted. Click the highlighted header to change the sort order.
costCenterIntro: Everything on this page is read from the local AI usage ledger (one row per model attempt: what it cost, and where that figure came from) together with the delivered-output records. Amounts stay separate per currency - no exchange rate is stored locally - so amounts in different currencies are never added together. With your own API key these amounts are estimates accounted from your provider's usage, not a charge made by CoolPilot.
costCenterLoadFailed: Could not read the cost ledger. The figures are unavailable, which is not the same as zero.
budgetIntro: This tab is the budget the pre-flight check reads: a natural calendar month (not the rolling window above), a ceiling you state in one currency, and what this process is currently holding for calls already in flight. Every figure is read from the local usage ledger - nothing here is estimated by the page.
budgetStatusUnavailable: Could not read the budget status. An unreadable figure is not zero, so no number is drawn.
budgetStatusPolicy: When a call would cross the limit
budgetPolicyWarn: Warn - allow the call and record it
budgetPolicyBlock: Block - refuse it before it is sent
budgetStatusUnknownCost: When the cost cannot be stated
budgetUnknownCostAllow: Allow (and count it as unpriced, never as 0)
budgetStatusStrategyInactive: In force only under "block" with a limit stated; under the current settings it changes no verdict.
budgetStrategyCostSaving: Cost-saving - keeps a line on the call and on the remainder
budgetStrategyBalanced: Balanced - goes to the limit and no further
budgetStrategyQualityFirst: Quality-first - does not stop early at zero headroom
budgetStrategyLineNone: Adds no line of its own: whether a call crosses is judged against the limit itself, and a pausable workflow stops only when nothing is left.
budgetStrategyStepStopDeclined: Adds no line of its own, and does not stop the next step early at zero headroom - what gets refused is the first call inside that crosses the limit.
budgetStrategyLineShares: Refuse a call whose upper bound crosses {call} of the limit, and stop a pausable workflow once less than {step} of it is left, keeping the remainder for smaller work.
budgetStatusSpentFloor: A floor, not a total: {unpriced} attempts had no price, {unmeasured} were never measured, and {otherCurrency} were billed in another currency ({currencies}).
budgetStatusTruncated: This period's ledger read hit its row ceiling, so the spending figure is a floor.
budgetStatusInFlight: {count} call(s) holding budget, counted across every process
budgetEnforcementTitle: What this check can and cannot promise
budgetEnforcementGuarantee: Enforcement level: {enforcement}. A call whose estimate plus this period's spending already crosses the limit is refused before it is sent, and the check and the hold it takes are one statement against the database every process shares - so two checks that overlap, in this process or in another one, cannot both pass. It is still not a hard cap: a hold that no call reports back from stops counting after its time-to-live, and a model with no price on file holds nothing at all.
budgetEnforcementUnknownCost: A model with no price on file holds nothing, because there is no honest amount to hold - the setting above decides whether it may run, and it is never treated as free.
budgetSettingsIntro: A limit is only comparable with costs quoted in the same currency, and this database holds no exchange rate, so the currency you pick is the one this period is added up in.
budgetSettingsLimitHint: Leave empty to state no ceiling. Empty is not 0 - 0 would read as "spend nothing".
budgetSettingsStrategyHint: The tier is in force only under "block" with a limit stated; warn and off are unaffected by it, and with no limit stated there is no line to cross. It changes only where the gate stops - not routing, retries, key rotation, or what a rewrite or an image call does.
budgetSettingsFormHint: Saving changes these five settings only: this page writes no ledger row and takes no hold. Calls already in flight keep the verdict they were granted.
budgetSaveFailed: Could not save the budget settings.
budgetLimitInvalid: The monthly limit must be a number, or empty for no ceiling.
budgetEstimateHint: Asks the server the same three questions the gate asks - price catalog, budget settings, this period's ledger - so a preview cannot disagree with the check that would refuse the call. Read-only: no hold, no ledger row, no stored text.
budgetEstimateTextHint: Measured for its token estimate and then dropped: never stored, never logged, never echoed back.
budgetEstimateTargetUnresolved: No model could be resolved before the call ({provider} / {model} as sent), so no price was looked up.
budgetEstimateRangeOpen: {currency} {min} or more (no reply ceiling stated, so no upper bound)
budgetEstimateUnpriced: The price catalog has nothing for this model and dimension - unpriced, which is not free.
budgetEstimateUnknown: What this call would be billed on cannot be stated, so there is no amount to show.
budgetEstimateTokens: Input at least {input} tokens, reply up to {output}.
budgetEstimateQuantityHint: Units of the dimension above (images, seconds, characters). It is what the catalog's unit price is multiplied by - nothing here fills it in for you.
budgetEstimateNumberInvalid: The quantity or the reply ceiling is not a number.
budgetDecisionDefinite: even the lower bound crosses the limit
budgetDecisionPossible: the upper bound crosses the limit
budgetDecisionStrategyLine: this tier's own line (the limit was not crossed)
budgetDecisionCounted: This estimate is counted in the totals above.
budgetDecisionNotCounted: This estimate counts toward no total - it states no amount, and is never added as 0.
budgetEstimateReadOnly: The verdict is as of now: between this answer and the real call the period's spending can grow, and only the call's own check decides.
budgetNoteOutputCeilingUnknown: No reply ceiling was stated, so the upper bound is not knowable.
budgetNoteRouteMayDiffer: The route was resolved before the call; the runtime may still change it.
budgetNoteRouteUnresolved: No model could be resolved for this call, so there was no price to look up.
budgetNoteUsageBasisUnknown: A per-unit dimension with no quantity stated: there is nothing to multiply.
budgetNotePriceNotOnFile: The catalog has nothing for this provider, model and dimension. Not free.
budgetNoteDimensionMismatch: The catalog priced a different dimension than the one about to be metered.
budgetNoteCurrencyMismatch: The price is quoted in another currency than the limit, and no exchange rate is stored, so the two are never subtracted.
budgetNoteSpendIncomplete: This period's spending includes a figure nobody could state.
budgetNoteSpendTruncated: This period's ledger read hit its row ceiling, so the spending figure is a floor.
budgetReasonOff: Control is off, so nothing was refused - the figures are still reported.
budgetReasonNoLimit: No limit is stated, so there is nothing to cross.
budgetReasonWithinLimit: The estimate stays inside the limit.
budgetReasonOverLimit: Even the lowest possible cost crosses the limit.
budgetReasonOverLimitWarning: The upper bound crosses the limit; a shorter reply would have fit.
budgetReasonUnknownCostNotCounted: The cost cannot be stated, so it was left out of every total rather than added as 0.
budgetReasonUnknownCostRefused: The cost cannot be stated, and the setting says to refuse such calls.
budgetReasonSpendIncomplete: This period contains a figure nobody could state, so the spending total is a floor.
budgetReasonCurrencyNotCompared: The price is in another currency than the limit, so no comparison was made.
budgetReasonHoldLost: The estimate and the period's spending had room, but by the time the hold was written another call had taken it.
budgetReasonCostSavingCallLine: The cost-saving tier stopped this call first: on its upper bound it would have spent over four fifths of the limit, and the limit itself was not crossed.
budgetReasonCostSavingRemainingLine: The cost-saving tier stopped this step first: under a fifth of this period's limit is left, and that remainder is kept for smaller work.
budgetReasonStepLineDeclined: The quality-first tier declines to stop this step at zero headroom; every call inside is still judged one by one, and the first that genuinely crosses the limit is refused.
qualityIntro: What this window measured, what one qualified output cost, and what the figures suggest. Every reading comes from records this install already keeps - the AI usage ledger and the content records - and where nothing was recorded the page says so instead of drawing a zero.
qualityWindow: Window: {from} - {to}, the same {days} days as the tabs beside it.
qualityLoading: Reading the quality and cost figures…
qualityLoadFailed: Could not read the quality and cost figures. An unreadable figure is not zero, so none is drawn.
qualityTruncated: This window's ledger read hit its row ceiling, so every count and amount below is a floor.
qualityMetricCallsNote: {requests} requests in total, {perCall} per call. A call is one business request with its retries counted as the same call.
qualityMetricFirstPassNote: {basis}. The call sent one request and it succeeded - no retry was needed. This is a request-level reading, not a content verdict.
qualityMetricFirstRequestNote: {basis}. The call's first request succeeded, whether or not a later one followed; the self-corrections this install cannot explain sit in the gap between this rate and the one above.
qualityMetricRetriesNote: {share} of the window's {requests} requests were not the first one of their call.
qualityMetricFailedCallsNote: No request of these calls succeeded. Each is counted as one call, however many requests it sent.
qualityMetricUnresolvedNote: A predecessor was recorded but is not among the rows this window read, so the retry is counted and left unclassified rather than guessed at.
qualityMetricAdoptionNote: {basis}. Adoption means the item reached "posted" - it was actually published. It says nothing about whether the content was any good.
qualityMetricHumanEditsNote: {basis}; the rest ({derived}) were produced by the platform adapter and never touched by hand.
qualityMetricEditMagnitudeNote: Not recorded anywhere: a rendition keeps that it was edited and when, never a before/after text, and the item's own update stamp moves for every write. This page will not invent a character count.
qualityMetricsSource: Sources: the AI usage ledger (one row per request) for the call figures, content_items.status for adoption, and the per-platform renditions for the edit signal. A call split by the window's edge is counted on both sides.
qualityMetricsNoQualityClaim: None of these is a quality score. A successful request is not a qualified output, and no model graded anything here.
qualityHumanEditsTruncated: The item scan hit its row ceiling, so the rendition counts above are floors.
qualityHumanEditsUnreadable: {count} stored rendition(s) could not be read by this build. They are counted, never dropped.
qualityObjectiveIntro: The optimisation objective: what the window's adopted outputs cost, per currency. "Qualified" means published - the only adoption signal this install records.
qualityObjectiveNone: The window has no amount to state in any currency, so there is no unit cost to show.
qualityObjectiveTokens: {tokens} ledger tokens per adopted output, retries included.
qualityObjectiveTokensNone: Tokens per adopted output: not measurable - the window adopted nothing to divide by.
qualityObjectiveAttributionNote: Attributed cost sums the requests that named one of these outputs; window cost is everything the window's ledger stated, including calls that belong to no output at all (research, chat, probes). Attribution is a sum over recorded ids, not a share allocated by a rule.
qualityObjectiveUnattributed: Not attributed to an adopted output: {amounts}
qualityObjectiveAttributionPartial: {adopted} outputs were adopted but only {attributed} could be read, so the attributed cost is a floor.
qualityObjectiveIncomplete: This figure is a floor: {unpriced} requests had no price and {unmeasured} were never measured.
qualitySuggestionsIntro: Each suggestion carries the figures it rests on, what applying it changes, and the risk it carries. Nothing here estimates a saving - no percentage of money has been verified.
qualitySuggestionsNone: The window's figures support no suggestion right now. That is a normal answer, not a missing one.
qualitySuggestionAppliedNote: Saved at {time}. Only the budget's execution tier was written: no model routing, no shorter replies, and no historical ledger row was touched. Seeing the cost and quality effect needs calls made after this moment - the figures above are the same window's measurements either way.
qualitySuggestionNotApplicable: Nothing was written: this suggestion's basis no longer holds, so the page did not apply a stale reading.
qualitySuggestionApplyFailed: Could not apply the suggestion. Nothing was written.
qualitySuggestionCostSavingTitle: Keep part of the limit in reserve
qualitySuggestionCostSavingBasis: {spent} of the {limit} limit is already spent ({share}), and the tier in force is "{strategy}".
qualitySuggestionCostSavingEffect: Switches the execution strategy to cost-saving: a call whose upper bound would take over four fifths of the limit is refused, and a pausable workflow stops once less than a fifth is left, so the remainder can pay for smaller work.
qualitySuggestionCostSavingRisk: Large calls can be refused below the limit, and a pausable workflow may stop earlier than it would otherwise. It changes no model, no reply length and no retry.
qualitySuggestionRecordPricesBasis: {unpriced} of the window's {requests} requests could not be priced: the catalog has nothing for that provider, model and dimension.
qualitySuggestionRecordPricesEffect: A price in the catalog lets those calls state an amount, which turns the totals on every cost tab from floors into totals.
qualitySuggestionRecordPricesRisk: Only you can state the price, and a wrong one is worse than a blank: the amount would be computed from it and shown as yours.
qualitySuggestionEnableBudgetBasis: The window accounted for {amount} across {requests} requests, and the budget policy is off - nothing is watching it.
qualitySuggestionEnableBudgetEffect: A policy of warn or block lets the gate judge each call against a stated ceiling before it is sent, and record what it decided.
qualitySuggestionEnableBudgetRisk: A ceiling is your number, not one this page may guess; under block, calls that would cross it are refused instead of sent.
qualitySuggestionFailedCallsTitle: Look into the failed and retried calls
qualitySuggestionFailedCallsBasis: {failed} of {calls} calls never succeeded, and {retries} of {requests} requests were retries. Passed on one request: {pass}.
qualitySuggestionFailedCallsEffect: Nothing automatic: no execution tier changes how a request is retried. The provider, key or prompt has to change, or the failure has to be accepted.
qualitySuggestionFailedCallsRisk: Acting on this means reading error summaries in the call ledger - the three tiers differ in where they stop, not in what they send.
qualitySuggestionAdoptionTitle: Most of the window's content was never published
qualitySuggestionAdoptionBasis: {adopted} of the {created} items created in the window reached "posted" ({rate}).
qualitySuggestionAdoptionEffect: Nothing automatic: adoption is a judgement about content, and this page scores nothing. It is raised because a low adoption rate makes every unit cost above a cost per draft rather than per used output.
qualitySuggestionAdoptionRisk: This is not evidence that the content was bad - it may be waiting, scheduled, or simply not published yet.
costCenterStatCostNote: Estimated from the price snapshot in force at call time (computed) or reported by the provider (provider-reported). A call whose price cannot be stated is never written as 0.
costCenterStatCostNone: No amount can be accounted for in this window
costCenterCostComplete: Every attempt in this window stated a figure, so the amounts above are totals.
costCenterCostPartial: {unpriced} attempts had no price and {unmeasured} were never measured, so the amounts above are partial, not totals.
costCenterStatTokensNote: Input {input} / output {output}. One row per model request, so retries are counted as well.
costCenterStatDeliveredNote: Successfully generated articles - the same definition the old usage page used.
costCenterStatAvgCostNote: Shown only when every attempt in the window stated a figure and at least one article was delivered; otherwise no estimate is made.
costCenterTrustCard: How far these figures can be trusted
costCenterTrustRetries: {count} of them were not the first request of their call. Key rotation, model fallback and self-correction retries all look like this, so this count is not a self-correction count.
costCenterSourcesNote: computed is our arithmetic over a price snapshot; provider-reported is the vendor's own charge; unpriced and unknown are rows where no figure may be stated at all.
costCenterBudgetNote: Estimates and budget control belong to P8-04 and are not built yet, so no budget figure is shown here.
costCenterPurposeNote: Grouped by the purpose recorded with each call. Group amounts ignore currency and are only meant for comparing groups against each other; quote the per-currency figures above instead.
costCenterTrendNote: Buckets are local calendar days, the same rule the range filter uses. Bar length is the accounted amount only; calls whose cost cannot be stated are counted and marked separately.
costCenterTrendEmpty: No ledger rows in this window
costCenterModelNote: Every model attempt, grouped by provider and model. A group that includes unpriced calls is marked, and its amount is a lower bound.
costCenterCatalogNote: A call in a dimension with no price in force is recorded as unpriced rather than 0. Prices are maintained under System, Model Management, Price list.
costCenterMeteringNote: Every dimension the ledger knows is listed, whether or not this window used it. Measured / unpriced / unstated are this window's own rows for that dimension; a dimension this runtime has no call path for is named here instead of quietly missing.
costCenterMeteringNoCalls: No calls of this dimension in the window.
costCenterMeteringAllStated: Every amount this dimension produced in the window could be stated.
costCenterMeteringNoPath: Cannot be metered: this runtime has no call path for this dimension.
costCenterMeteringThroughText: Metered as the text rows of its calls (agent / workflow nodes).
costCenterReasonNoPrice: No price in force for this provider + model + dimension.
costCenterReasonPriceKind: A price answered, but it prices another dimension.
costCenterReasonPriceUnit: The price row states no unit rate to multiply.
costCenterReasonNoUsage: The provider reported no usage for this request.
costCenterReasonQuantityMissing: No amount was recorded for the unit this dimension is priced in.
costCenterReasonQuantityUnit: The amount was recorded under a unit this dimension does not price.
costCenterReasonQuantityUnusable: The amount recorded for this dimension is not a usable number.
costCenterReasonFailed: The request did not succeed, so no usage arrived to measure.
costCenterReasonInterrupted: The call was interrupted: what arrived may be less than what was billed.
costCenterReasonNotRecorded: The ledger kept no reason for this row (it predates this reading).
costCenterLegacyNote: The old usage-page figures, kept as the delivered-output side of the same window.
costCenterCallsIntro: Per-call detail: one row per request the runtime actually sent - failures and retries included, each on its own row. The retry type is read from the request that came before it, never from the attempt number, because a rotated key, a demoted model and a self-correction all look the same in a number.
costCenterCallsFilterNote: Filters change which requests are listed. The call column always describes the whole call as it appears in this window, so a filter can never make a call look like it sent fewer requests than it did.
costCenterCallsMatched: {attempts} requests matched the filters; {retries} of them were not the first request of their call.
costCenterCallsMatchedCost: Accounted amount for the matched requests
costCenterCallsMatchedNoCost: No matched request can state an amount
costCenterCallsScanNote: This window holds more than {limit} ledger rows. Only the newest part was read, so older rows are not included in these figures.
costCenterCallsTraceCapNote: Some content / task links were left unresolved because this answer's lookup budget was spent; those rows show the recorded id instead.
costCenterCallsTableNote: Newest call first; inside one call the requests read in the order they were sent. Status and completeness are shown as the ledger stores them (success / failed / interrupted, reported / partial / unknown) rather than translated, so the screen and the database say the same word.
costCenterCallsEmpty: No request in this window matches these filters.
costCenterCallsGroupTitle: The call this request belongs to
costCenterCallsGroupLine: This call sent {attempts} request(s) in this window, {failed} of which did not succeed. This is request {index}.
costCenterCallsGroupCost: Accounted amount for the whole call
costCenterCallsGroupCostBound: At least one request of this call cannot state an amount, so the call's total is a lower bound.
costCenterCallsRetrySelfCorrection: Self-correction: the previous request succeeded and the call asked again
costCenterCallsRetryAfterFailed: Followed a request that did not succeed
costCenterCallsRetryUnresolved: The previous request is outside this window, so the retry type cannot be stated
costCenterCallsRetryChanged: Differs from the previous request in: {fields}
costCenterCallsRetrySame: Same identity as the previous request (provider, model, endpoint and key label all unchanged)
costCenterCallsPricingTitle: Pricing rule (the snapshot frozen onto this row)
costCenterCallsPricingToken: input {input} / million tokens · output {output} / million tokens
costCenterCallsPricingNone: No price snapshot on this row, which is why it states no amount
costCenterCallsDurationUnmeasured: not measured - the ledger does not time individual requests yet, and 0 does not mean instant
costCenterCallsTraceContentMissing: the recorded content id no longer exists in the content table
costCenterCallsTraceContentNone: this row named no content item
costCenterCallsTraceTaskNone: the id this row recorded resolves to no task
costCenterCallsByContentNote: Every content item this window's requests named, with what its calls added up to - retries included. Rows that named no content item are grouped as unclassified rather than left out; a group that cannot state every amount is marked and its figure is a lower bound. This table follows the window, not the table's filters.
costCenterCallsRawNote: Amounts here are accounted from your provider's reported usage and the price snapshot in force at call time (computed), or from the provider's own figure (provider-reported) - never from a charge CoolPilot made. A request whose price is unknown stays unpriced and is counted, not written as 0.
costCenterRunsTitle: Cost by run and node (Agent / Workflow)
costCenterRunsNote: Every execution this window's requests recorded, with what each of its nodes cost. A request that failed is counted with the amount it reported, not treated as free. The run's total is the sum of the node rows below, each row counted once, so the headline can be checked against the detail. Amounts stay per currency, and a reading whose rows could not all state a figure is marked as a lower bound. This table follows the window, not the table's filters.
costCenterRunsFailureCost: Money on requests that did not succeed
costCenterRunsColUnresolved: ({count} of them without a visible predecessor)
costCenterRunsRetryOverlap: A request can be both a repeat and unsuccessful, so those two amounts are two readings of the same requests and are never added together - the run total is the bill.
costCenterRunsUnresolvedNote: {count} repeated request(s) recorded a predecessor that was not among the rows this answer read. They are still counted as repeated requests, but what they repeated cannot be stated from here.
costCenterExtensionsNote: Every request in this window, added up per extension. An extension id comes from a real record: a published position (the same position-... id the app-store mine tab lists) or a built-in catalogue agent id the storefront really publishes. A request that names neither is kept as unattributed rather than given a plausible-looking name. Amounts are per currency and a failed request is counted at the amount it reported; a reading that leaves a request without a figure is marked as a lower bound. The repeated-request amount and the unsuccessful-request amount are two readings of the same requests and are never added together. This table follows the window and does not move with the filters above.
costCenterExtensionsRetryOverlap: A request can be both a repeated request and an unsuccessful one, so those two amounts are two readings of the same requests and are never added together - the amount column is that extension's bill.
costCenterExtensionsUnattributedNote: Unattributed is not an error: a chat answer, a transcription, an image or a rewrite belongs to no extension, and only a request really sent as a listed extension is counted under it.
dashboardDescription: Quickly review sites, content, runs, and schedules.
siteAddDialogHint: Only the site name and platform are required.
sitePlatformUrlHint: Changing the platform fills its standard website URL. You can edit the URL before creating the site.
sitesSidebarHint: Use @ in chat to tell the agent which site to control.
siteTakeoverHint: Take over Chrome on the right. This app does not store passwords.
noActiveBrowser: Choose a site and open Browser to stream Chrome here.
browserWaiting: Browser is ready, waiting for preview frames...
browserClosed: Browser is closed. Open Chrome to continue.
browserOpenedNotice: Browser tab opened. Use the right panel to take over login or watch agent actions.
error_AI_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_INVALID: AI provider returned invalid structured output
error_AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: The AI budget refused this call before it was sent. Raise the budget, then continue - a paused run keeps the work it finished.
error_MODEL_GATEWAY_MISSING_COOKIE: Model gateway session cookie is missing

openAIImageBaseUrlHint: Independent of the text service. Empty means "not configured": without a URL there is no image endpoint, and an image request fails with its own error instead of using the text endpoint.
modelListHint: Model options are fetched from the provider API and cached briefly.
aiRegistryDescription: Every model the runtime knows about, grouped by provider, with the capabilities it provides and the source of that claim. Only callable models are routed to.
aiRegistrySyncHint: Pick a provider, then sync to pull its live catalog. Your endpoints, enabled models and probed capabilities are kept.
aiRegistryEmpty: No model matches the current filters.
aiRegistrySetDefault: The router uses these first. Setting a default also enables that model.
aiRegistrySources: The letter on each chip shows where the capability came from - vendor metadata, local catalog rules, a probe or your own override.
aiProvidersDescription: A provider is a vendor with one callable endpoint. The key lives in the local credential vault - the database only keeps its reference.
aiProvidersApiKeyHint: One key per line (commas work too) - calls rotate through them and cool a key down after a 429. Stored encrypted on this machine; leave empty to keep the current keys.
aiProvidersKeyResetDone: Key reset - it is back in rotation
aiProvidersKeychainUnavailable: The OS keychain backend is not wired up yet, so keys are stored as an AES-256-GCM file inside the app data directory. That protects against accidental sharing, not against a local attacker.
modelPriceDescription: What one request costs, and since when. A price is never edited: a change adds a new row with a later effective time, so a call recorded last month keeps the figure it was costed with.
modelPriceEstimateNotice: A figure computed from this catalog is our arithmetic on your usage - an estimate, not a charge a provider confirmed. The ledger keeps the two apart and marks computed figures as such.
modelPriceProviderHint: The id the runtime signs with, for example gemini, groq, openai or openrouter.
modelPriceModelHint: * prices every model of this provider that has no row of its own.
modelPriceCachedHint: Leave this empty when the provider does not price cached input separately. Empty is not 0.
modelPriceVersionHint: Names this revision on every ledger row it costs, for example 2026-10.
modelPriceEffectiveHint: A call is costed with the newest price already in force when it started. A price that takes effect later never restates calls that already happened.
modelPriceDeclaredFreeHint: Only when every rate is a real 0. A rate nobody filled in is refused instead of being stored as free.
modelPriceFormHint: One row states one dimension: token rates for a token-metered dimension, a unit and its price for everything else. A row can never carry both - the catalog refuses it, because a price per image multiplied by a token count is not a figure anyone could read.
modelPriceSaved: Price added. Ledger rows already written keep the figure they were recorded with.
modelPriceSaveFailed: The price could not be added.
modelPriceHistoryEmpty: No price on file yet. Until one is added, every request reports that its cost cannot be stated, instead of reporting 0.
modelPriceUnpricedHint: These dimensions can appear in the ledger but have no price on file, so their cost stays blank rather than 0.
modelPriceUnitLabelHint: What this dimension is priced per. Changing the dimension re-seats it, because the catalog only accepts the units a dimension is actually billed in.
modelPriceUnitPriceHint: An empty box is "not stated": the row is refused instead of being stored as a free or 0 rate.
error_AI_PRICE_INVALID: This is not a price a request could be costed with
error_AI_PRICE_CONFLICT: That provider, model and dimension already has a price in force from that instant
